title: ai hooks and guard hardening
lead: `ai hooks --install --force` gets a merge rule that never duplicates the slicer group and never drops a non-slicer handler; a symlinked or directory `settings.json` is refused with code `state` and tested; `_glob_could_match_json` becomes a short conservative rule with the same verdicts on every glob the tests name.
findings_note: Deferred `later` follow-ups from the s439 relay review (release 1.18.0), 2026-11-02: `ai hooks --install --force` duplicates or drops handlers, untested symlink and directory settings paths, and an over-built Grep glob judgement in the guard.
boundary: **Not in this slice:** the plain `--install` refusal without `--force` (unchanged); the slicer-handler predicate (a `command` containing `slicer ai getting-started` or `slicer ai guard`, unchanged); de-duplicating exact snippet groups a user already has twice; `.claude` existing as a regular file; `settings.local.json` or `~/.claude`; any other guard verdict; Codex or Grok hooks.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Size M rather than S: three independent changes (a merge rule with several cases, a new refusal, a rewrite of the glob judgement) each need their own tests, though all live in `cmd_ai_hooks`, `ai.py` and tests/test_ai_hooks.py.

Verified against main at 50bd033 on 2026-11-02 by running `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer ai hooks --install` in scratch projects:

1. `cmd_ai_hooks` (src/slicer/cli.py:1079-1131) treats a group as installed when its `hooks` equal the snippet's handlers, and as a conflict when any handler's `command` contains a slicer command but the list differs. With `--force`, each conflicting group is replaced whole by the snippet group (`groups[i] = copy.deepcopy(wanted[0])`). Two faults follow:
   - Dropped handlers: a PreToolUse group `{"matcher": "Read|Grep|Edit|Write", "hooks": [{"command": "my-lint"}, {"command": "slicer ai guard", "timeout": 10}]}` came back holding only the slicer handler; `my-lint` was gone.
   - Duplicates: an exact snippet group plus a second group `{"matcher": "Bash", "hooks": [{"command": "slicer ai guard --old"}]}` came back as two identical snippet groups. Every conflicting group becomes a full copy, whether or not an exact group already exists. A later run then reports "already installed" and keeps both.
2. Settings path checks: `target.parent.is_symlink() or target.is_symlink()` refuses a symlinked `.claude` or `settings.json` with `StateError` (default code `state`, exit 2, "refusing a symlink settings path; nothing was written"). The probe confirmed both. Only the `.claude` directory symlink is tested (`test_AiHooksInstall_SymlinkToHome_IsRefused`); the `settings.json` file symlink is not. A directory at `.claude/settings.json` passes `target.exists()`, then `jsonio.read` raises `IsADirectoryError`, which `cmd_ai_hooks` does not catch: the probe got exit 3, code `io`, message "[Errno 21] Is a directory: '...'", without the usual "nothing was written". That is a user-fixable layout problem, not an internal failure, so this slice refuses it with `state` like the symlink case. (Owner may prefer to keep `io`; the spec assumes `state`.)
3. `_glob_could_match_json` (ai.py:34-75) tokenises brackets, walks the glob backwards against `.json` keeping a set of positions, and carries brace alternatives on a stack of position sets: about 40 lines for a check the s439 spec states in one clause ("when `tool_input.glob` ... could match a denied file"). A shorter conservative rule gives the same verdict on every glob `test_AiGuard_GrepGlob_DeniesPossibleJsonAndAllowsMarkdown` and `test_AiGuard_CaseVariants_DeniesTrackingPaths` name. Expand braces into alternatives (nested braces allowed, at most 64; more is treated as could-match). For each alternative, let T be the text after its last `*`, `?`, `[` or `]` (the whole alternative when it has none). It could match when T ends with `.json` or `.json` ends with T. Worked through the asserted globs: denied `*.json`, `**/*.json`, `s[0-9]*.[j]son` (T `son`), `*` and `config.*` (T empty), `????.json`, `*.{md,json}`, `**/*.{js,{md,json}}`, `*.JSON` (the caller casefolds); allowed `*.md`, `**/*.txt`, `*.jsonl`, `*.json.bak`, `*.{md,txt}`. The rule may deny a few globs the current code allows (for example `*.[!j]son`), which is the safe direction for a guard.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
- `src/slicer/cli.py` `cmd_ai_hooks`:
  - Before reading, refuse `target.exists() and not target.is_file()` with `StateError(f"{target}: not a regular file; nothing was written")` (code `state`), after the symlink check.
  - Merge rule with `--force`, per event, in this order. (a) A slicer handler is a dict whose `command` is a string containing `slicer ai getting-started` or `slicer ai guard`. (b) An exact group is one whose `hooks` equals the snippet's handlers, whatever its matcher. (c) A conflicting group is any other group holding at least one slicer handler. (d) Each conflicting group loses its slicer handlers; its other handlers and other keys (matcher included) keep their content and order; a group left with no handlers is removed. (e) If no exact group exists, the snippet group goes where the first conflicting group stood, replacing it if it was removed and directly after it if it survived. With no conflicting group, it is appended as today. Without `--force`, behaviour is unchanged: any conflicting group refuses with `state` and nothing is written.
  - `ai hooks` parser description: replace "Conflicting slicer hooks are refused unless --force" with a sentence saying `--force` removes other slicer handlers and keeps every other handler.
- `src/slicer/ai.py`: `_glob_could_match_json` rewritten to the rule above, with a small brace-expansion helper. It stays free of state imports and never lists files.
- `tests/test_ai_hooks.py`: the tests below. Every existing test in the file passes unchanged, including `test_AiHooksInstall_Force_ReplacesTheSlicerGroupInPlace` (a group holding only a slicer handler is removed and the snippet takes its slot) and `test_AiHooksInstall_EqualHandlers_IsAlreadyInstalled`.
- `docs/commands.md` row `ai hooks [--install] [--force]` and the `ai hooks` merge paragraph in `docs/agents.md`: state rule (d)-(e) and the directory refusal. `CHANGELOG.md` `## [Unreleased]` `### Fixed`.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `tests/test_ai_hooks.py`:
- `test_AiHooksInstall_ForceMixedGroup_KeepsUserHandlers`: a PreToolUse group holding `my-lint` and an old guard handler (`timeout` 99). After `--install --force`, PreToolUse is `[{"matcher": "Read|Grep|Edit|Write", "hooks": [my-lint]}, SNIPPET_GROUP]` and SessionStart is added. Fails today (`my-lint` dropped).
- `test_AiHooksInstall_ForceWithExactGroup_RemovesOtherSlicerHandlersWithoutDuplicating`: an exact snippet group plus a `Bash` group whose only handler is `{"command": "slicer ai guard", "timeout": 5}`. After `--force`, PreToolUse holds exactly one snippet group and no `Bash` group. Fails today (two snippet groups).
- `test_AiHooksInstall_ForceTwice_IsIdempotent`: after one `--force` on the mixed fixture, a second `--install --force` and a plain `--install` report `written: []` and leave the bytes unchanged.
- `test_AiHooksInstall_SymlinkedSettingsFile_IsStateAndWritesNothing`: `.claude/settings.json` is a symlink to a file outside the project. Exit 2, code `state`, the message names the path, and the link target's bytes are unchanged. Passes today; it pins the behaviour.
- `test_AiHooksInstall_DirectoryAtSettingsPath_IsStateAndWritesNothing`: `.claude/settings.json` is a directory. Exit 2, code `state`, the message names the path and says nothing was written, and the snapshot is unchanged. Fails today (exit 3, `io`).
- `test_AiGuard_GlobJudgement_IsTheTailRule`: calls `ai._glob_could_match_json` directly. Every glob already asserted (both lists in `test_AiGuard_GrepGlob_DeniesPossibleJsonAndAllowsMarkdown`) keeps its verdict. A brace pattern with more than 64 alternatives returns True. An unbalanced `{` does not raise. Mutation-check by flipping the `.json`-ends-with-T clause.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. Write the tests; confirm the mixed-group, duplicate and directory tests fail.
2. Directory refusal; then the `--force` merge rule as a small helper inside cli.py, used only by `cmd_ai_hooks`.
3. Rewrite `_glob_could_match_json`; run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -k '*AiGuard*'` with no edits to existing guard tests.
4. Help text, docs and CHANGELOG.

Owner decisions: a directory at `.claude/settings.json` is refused with code `state` (exit 2), not `io` (confirmed 2026-11-02).

sections.heading: Check
sections.body:
- [ ] `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests -k '*AiHooks*'` and `-k '*AiGuard*'` pass, and `git diff main -- tests/test_ai_hooks.py` shows only added tests (no existing test edited).
- [ ] In a scratch project, the mixed-group and exact-plus-old fixtures behave as in Failing tests under `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m slicer ai hooks --install --force`, and a directory at `.claude/settings.json` exits 2 with code `state`.
- [ ] `_glob_could_match_json` is shorter than the current 42 lines (ai.py:34-75) including its helper.
- [ ] `python3 tests/affected.py --run`, the full suite, `slicer check` and `git diff --check` pass.
